hits.snippet: My third startup company was based on an amazing sensor technology that became a standard for measurement of large manufactured products like aircraft and automobiles. We worked with BMW to mount that sensor on robotic arms on their X5 line to monitor and correct dimensional problems they were having. We succeeded with the monitoring part of that, but making on-the-fly adjustments to robot programs in the line was deemed too risky. Fifteen years later, I got a call from Duke University about a breakthrough in robotic motion planning. I flew down, met the inventors, and saw something that could fundamentally change how robots could move and adapt safely. The importance of the breakthrough and the quality of the inventor team was enough.
